query: US-Iran conflict status July 2026: is there a ceasefire in effect? Latest on Islamabad MoU, tit-for-tat strikes, Trump statements, negotiations after July 11 2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here is a summary of what I found:

## Answer: No ceasefire is in effect as of mid-July 2026

The **Islamabad MoU ceasefire has collapsed**. Key findings:

**Ceasefire status:** Trump declared the MoU "over" on July 8, 2026. Iran's Foreign Ministry announced July 13 it would no longer comply, accusing the US of "openly violating it." Both sides are trading active strikes.

**The Islamabad MoU:** A 14-point framework signed June 17, 2026 (Trump at Versailles post-G7; Pezeshkian in Tehran; Pakistan-brokered). It provided a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopened the Strait of Hormuz toll-free, ended the US blockade, and waived oil sanctions—but deferred all nuclear, missile, and regional-ally issues.

**Tit-for-tat strikes (July 11+):** US struck for four consecutive nights (July 11–14), hitting 140 Iranian targets July 11 alone. Iran attacked ~7 commercial vessels, hit US/allied bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. The US reimposed its naval blockade at 4pm ET July 14. Strait crossings collapsed to 22 ships (vs. 147 pre-war).

**Trump statements:** Threatened (July 14) to strike Iranian power plants and bridges "next week" unless Iran negotiates; floated then reversed a 20% Strait transit fee; pivoted to seeking Gulf-state US investment deals.

**Negotiations after July 11:** Not fully ruled out—Qatar and Pakistan are mediating. Qatar's FM said ceasefire talks would resume after Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's funeral. CFR assessed the deal has collapsed, leaving the US "few good options."

Note: AskNews tools were unavailable (inactive subscription), so I relied on web search plus WebFetch of Wikipedia, NPR, CBS, CNN, Al Jazeera, Axios, CNBC, and CFR (all July 13–14, 2026 vintage). Full structured findings with 12 data points and 12 sources have been submitted.

key_facts: No functioning ceasefire is in effect as of mid-July 2026; the Islamabad MoU has collapsed.
Trump declared the Islamabad MoU 'over' on July 8, 2026, calling the Iranian regime 'sick people.'
The Islamabad Memorandum (14-point framework) was signed June 17, 2026 by Trump and Iranian President Pezeshkian, brokered by Pakistan with Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt.
The MoU provided a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopened the Strait of Hormuz toll-free for 60 days, ended the US naval blockade, and waived (not eliminated) oil sanctions for 60 days.
The MoU deferred all hard issues: no accord on Iran's nuclear program/uranium, ballistic missiles, or regional allies.
On July 13, 2026, Iran's Foreign Ministry (spokesman Esmail Baghaei) announced Iran would no longer comply with the MoU, accusing the US of 'openly violating it.'
On July 11, 2026 the US said it hit 140 Iranian military targets in its third round of strikes that week, following a merchant-ship attack in the Strait of Hormuz.
US struck Iran for four consecutive nights (July 11-14); Iran attacked ~7 commercial vessels over the week and hit US/allied bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan.
The US reimposed its naval blockade of Iranian ports at 4 p.m. ET on July 14, 2026.
Strait of Hormuz crossings collapsed to 22 ships on July 9 vs 147 before the February war.
Trump threatened on July 14 to strike Iranian power plants and bridges 'next week' unless Iran negotiates.
Trump floated then reversed a 20% Strait cargo/transit fee, pivoting to Gulf-state US investment deals.
Diplomacy continues behind the scenes via Qatar and Pakistan; Qatar's FM said ceasefire talks would resume after Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's funeral.
The '2026 Iran war' began Feb 28, 2026 with US/Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and negotiator Ali Larijani.
An earlier two-week ceasefire was agreed April 7-8, 2026 and extended 'indefinitely' by Trump on April 21, but was repeatedly violated.
